newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's gas committee mulls supply applications.
newsitem.headline: Norway's gas committee mulls supply applications.

text.p: Applications to deliver new gas to continental Europe from 1999 have been submitted by 13 licence groups to Norway's Gas Supply Committee (FU), Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.

Gas needs to be allocated to the Troll sales agreements, the planned power station at Kaarstoe north of Stavanger, a contract with Germany's Ruhrgas and a recently sealed deal with Italian gas company SNAM.
No decision has been taken yet on the size of supplies to be allocated in this round, and some of the contracts may be postponed until next year, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Annual deliveries of 20 billion cubic metres have to be placed with supply fields, which will put Norway's total yearly gas exports in 2005 at a plateau of about 70 billion cubic metres.
The possible purchase of Norwegian gas by the Czech Repoublic would come on top of this, Statoil said.
The FU has until May 1 to analyse field and transport solutions before submitting its recommendations of volumes and fields to the Ministry of Petroleum and Energy.
